The Nissan Terrano Is Making a Comeback in China, but This Is What America Is Getting
6 photos
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information China
Nissan is reviving the Terrano nameplate as a boxy, ladder-frame, off-road SUV. Regulatory filings from China's Ministry of Industry and Information have leaked the production model with three distinct powertrain options. The model will not come to America, but Nissan also has something in store for the American market.
Every version of the revived SUV comes equipped with a mechanical, driveshaft-based four-wheel-drive system, shared with the Nissan Navara Pro PHEV pickup truck. That is the model that it also shares the engine lineup, too.
The range starts with the 2.3-liter four-cylinder unit, which delivers 187 horsepower (190 metric horsepower). Higher in the range sits the 2.0-liter inline-four, factory-rated at 254 horsepower (258 metric horsepower).
The plug-in-hybrid variant is the range-topping Terrano, pairing a 204-horsepower (207-metric-horsepower) 2.0-liter turbo gas engine and an electric motor for a combined output of up to 268 horsepower (272 metric horsepower). The official rating of the PHEV has yet to be disclosed.
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information China The production SUV closely follows the rugged styling of the Terrano PHEV Concept, revealed earlier this year. Expectedly, it will get the boxy styling, with an upright front end, robust wheel arches, heavy cladding, and bold Nissan lettering above the grille. A side-opening tailgate holds the spare tire in typical off-roader fashion.
The model measures 200.7 inches (5,098 millimeters) in length, 77.9 inches (1,979 millimeters) in width, and 77.2 inches (1,961 millimeters) in height, sitting on a wheelbase of 112.2 inches (2,450 millimeters).
The Terrano will ride on 18-inch wheels as standard, but larger 19-inch units will be available at an extra cost. Customers will be able to choose from various trims, spare-wheel covers, and wheel designs and will also have a panoramic sunroof available for the top trim.
The production Terrano is expected to officially debut in China before April 2027. Built in partnership with Dongfeng in China, the model will also make it to Australia, Japan, and potentially India in right-hand-drive form.
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information China The Nissan Terrano will not set wheels on American soil. The Terrano is produced in China through Nissan’s joint venture with Dongfeng, which makes exports to China widely impossible. However, North America is expected to receive a separate Xterra revival instead.
Xterra is already in development. Once it’s ready, the body-on-frame model will enter production at Nissan’s assembly plant in Canton, Mississippi. Production is scheduled to begin in 2028, putting the rugged SUV on the exact same assembly plant where the previous generation was built before its 2015 discontinuation.
The Xterra will get completely different powertrains. While the Terrano will hit the market with four-cylinder gas, diesel, and plug-in hybrid setups, the U.S.-bound Xterra will feature V6 and V6 hybrid powertrains, compliant with the stricter local emission regulations, CarBuzz reports . The Nissan SUV will give rivals such as the Toyota Land Cruiser and Ford Bronco a run for their money.
